data.content_ref: inline:The necessity of separation (SRC_005) depends on the assumption that neural weights are the sole source of systemic bias. This relation is refuted if a single engine, when coupled with an external symbolic verifier (as mentioned in SRC_003 counterconditions), achieves the same verification reliability as two separate neural engines, thereby proving that the 'blind spot' is a property of the probabilistic method, not the engine count.
